Goal: I can choose a convenient coordinate setup to prove a general result.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A coordinate proof of a general fact uses variables, placed to keep the algebra simple.

Theorem: the diagonals of a rectangle are equal. Place the rectangle at O(0, 0), A(a, 0), B(a, b), C(0, b). Then OB = √(a2 + b2) and AC = √((0 − a)2 + (b − 0)2) = √(a2 + b2). So OB = AC, for every rectangle at once.

Good habits: put a vertex at the origin, a side on an axis, and use 2a, 2b when midpoints are coming.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Why might you label a vertex (2a, 0) instead of (a, 0)?
slides.reveal: So that midpoints come out as whole variables like (a, 0), with no fractions.
